issues.description: Bounded package metadata confirms a readable firm-identifier CSV with a physical gvkey header, but it did not inspect row values, firm coverage, or periods. Validate that coverage against the actual consumer during panel preparation. Do not infer that this separate list must itself supply permno and year without a specific consumer contract.

The SEC filings route and form-period selection are documented, but the required filing population, local document coverage, and resulting text-section coverage have not been verified for the construction period.

The supplied EDGAR disclosure stage is part of the documented workflow and the final merge consumes its annual disclosure products. Confirm the producer's exact output names, fields, identifier keys, and construction history from an approved complete source view before treating those products as ready.

The index and feature stages use configured paths whose alignment with the checked workspace and the documented downstream paths has not been verified. Configure the expected layout and confirm the producer-consumer paths before running those stages.
The ownership workflow has distinct raw and cleaned outputs; confirm that the configured producer paths resolve to the paths consumed by the annual stock-characteristics merge.

The annual stock-characteristics stage reads ownership_SAS_output.csv, but its exact producer, columns, identifier keys, and year coverage are not established. Confirm a compatible author-prepared/local output and its contract; no SAS execution was used to infer it.

The older Good Jobs First snapshot and crosswalk feed a column-difference diagnostic, not the annual analytical product, but the supplied unedited script reads them. To run that script unchanged, provide both files at the expected paths; alternatively, an owner-reviewed change may skip only these unused diagnostic reads. No such edit is applied or assumed here.

The reviewed workflow defines final joins on gvkey/permno/year or gvkey/year and constructs one- through four-year leads. Check key uniqueness, observed period coverage, and lead availability as ordinary validation after the separate inputs are prepared; those empirical results are not shown by bounded package metadata and do not by themselves imply a missing input.

Catalog records identify candidate Compustat, CRSP, Revelio, Refinitiv, Sustainalytics, and RepRisk tables, but do not establish all consumer-required column names, identifier mappings, duplicate handling, and period coverage. Confirm those specific schemas against each separate input and link table before combining them.

The final merge consumes dei_esg_hiring_annual.RDS, but no producer or compatible field/key/history contract is established in the reviewed workflow. Confirm the supplied author-prepared product or its supported producer before treating this required final input as available.

The sentence-topic stage supplies an intermediate, but the final topic-fraction cleaner's implementation is wholly withheld from the safe view. Its exact input/output fields, firm-year keys, and construction/history contract remain unknown; confirm those details before treating sentence_topic_mention_fraction_20topics.RDS as produced.

The datasheet documents the Twitter source, and the workflow has separate handle, raw, feature, and firm-link artifacts. Their exact schemas, population/time coverage, feature construction, and company-link keys cannot be confirmed from the wholly withheld Twitter program bodies; use compatible author-prepared/local artifacts and confirm those specific contracts.

A current public academic-use Loughran–McDonald dictionary is a supported route and documents seven sentiment category identifiers. The exact consumer-required category fields and definitions still need to be mapped to the supplied sentence-feature code; the revision label alone is not treated as a missing-data or byte-identity gate.

The workflow names a Feather corpus input and the all-mpnet-base-v2 sentence model, but corpus columns and period, exact feature/topic output schema, and local NLTK/model-resource availability have not been verified. Confirm the consumer fields and existing compatible resources before running the sentence branch.

The master includes a Revelio annual-construction stage and the final merge consumes a diversity-metrics annual RDS. The reviewed source evidence establishes the monthly Revelio field selection and final consumption, but does not bind that producer to the exact final input path/schema. Confirm the producer output path, fields, and period from the approved safe producer view before treating that RDS as a generated dependency.

The pinned safe view of the cleaning master script is wholly withheld. The frozen dependency list records seven producer/merge include edges for Compustat, CRSP, Revelio, stock/ownership, ESG, Good Jobs First, and the final merge, but no literal call or execution order is visible to verify those edges from the master. The package inventory lists the producer sources, and separately reviewed stage code supports producer/product facts; neither proves that the hidden master calls them. Exact master calls and ordering remain unresolved, and no output or order is inferred from filenames or the ledger alone.

evidence.description: The Good Jobs First constructor selects penalty and offense fields and annualizes employment and discrimination measures.
evidence.quote:
# Select only discrimination-based offenses
goodjobsfirst_annual <- goodjobsfirst_to_merge %>% 
  select(gvkey, pen_year, penalty_adjusted, primary_offense, offense_group) %>%
  rename(year = pen_year)

# Annualize data
goodjobsfirst_annual <- goodjobsfirst_annual %>%
  group_by(gvkey, year) %>%
  summarise(total_employment_penalties = sum(penalty_adjusted*as.numeric(offense_group == 'employment-related offenses'), na.rm = T),
            total_discrimination_penalties = sum(penalty_adjusted*as.numeric(primary_offense == 'employment discrimination'), na.rm = T),  
            number_employment_penalities = sum(as.numeric(offense_group == 'employment-related offenses'), na.rm = T),
            number_discrimination_penalties = sum(as.numeric(primary_offense == 'employment discrimination'), na.rm = T),
            count = n()) %>%

  select(unique_id, unique_id_new, permno, gvkey)
# Convert to common data types for linking
sustainalytics_linktable <- sustainalytics_linktable %>%
  mutate(unique_id = as.character(unique_id),
         unique_id_new = as.character(unique_id_new))
sustainalytics_weighted_scores <- sustainalytics_weighted_scores %>%
  mutate(unique_id = as.character(unique_id),
         unique_id_new = as.character(unique_id_new))
# UNIQUE_ID + UNIQUE_ID_new unique identifier in sustainalytics_linktable (but not unique in sustainalytics_raw for UNIQUE_ID %in% c(0, 20, 50, 70)

sustainalytics_weighted_scores <- sustainalytics_weighted_scores %>%
  inner_join(sustainalytics_linktable, by = c('unique_id', 'unique_id_new'))

evidence.description: The final merge creates consecutive-year lead/lag flags through five years.

mutate(good_lead_1 = coalesce(if_else(lead(year, 1) == year + 1, 1, 0), 0),
         good_lead_2 = coalesce(if_else(lead(year, 2) == year + 2, 1, 0), 0),
         good_lead_3 = coalesce(if_else(lead(year, 3) == year + 3, 1, 0), 0),
         good_lead_4 = coalesce(if_else(lead(year, 4) == year + 4, 1, 0), 0),
         good_lead_5 = coalesce(if_else(lead(year, 5) == year + 5, 1, 0), 0)) %>% 
  # make variables indicating if they are good lags
  mutate(good_lag_1 = coalesce(if_else(lag(year, 1) == year - 1, 1, 0), 0),
         good_lag_2 = coalesce(if_else(lag(year, 2) == year - 2, 1, 0), 0),
         good_lag_3 = coalesce(if_else(lag(year, 3) == year - 3, 1, 0), 0),
         good_lag_4 = coalesce(if_else(lag(year, 4) == year - 4, 1, 0), 0),

review_notes: The assessment used the coordinator-pinned, independently verified safe source views. Protected authentication, connection, endpoint, and private configuration blocks were withheld; all Twitter source bodies were wholly withheld. The reviewed source programs remain present in the package. These view limits are implementation-review limits, not findings that source code or data are absent, and no credential validity, use, or effect is inferred.

A configured relative sentence-corpus filepath was reviewed for producer-consumer alignment; its value is omitted. This is ordinary workflow path metadata and does not create a separate entitlement or original-path identity condition.

One current-turn Sustainalytics lookup stdout was overwritten before its first bytes were separately preserved. No first-output, argv, or wrapper reconstruction is claimed; only the surviving current capture is used as evidence.
No author code, model, or SAS execution/import/compilation, package installation, payload download, API query, external contact, or applied source edit was performed.

Generated intermediates are accounted for through their supplied producers and do not have to pre-exist before the full pipeline runs. Remaining requirements are raw inputs or final products whose producer contracts remain specifically unresolved.

Source evidence metadata was rechecked against the coordinator-pinned safe views. Exact visible nonsecret fragments are quoted with original one-based line numbers; configured or structurally distributed statements are cited by the in-work safe-view hash. Redacted path values and unverified producer-output identity are not reconstructed.

Base Python and R availability uses the original registered successful environment proof. Python distribution rows use a shape-normalized copy of the saved successful typed capture; no package was installed, loaded, or newly checked.
